_meta.description: Household-scale assumptions for Griddy Home (California). Each entry uses the common shape {value, units, kind, source, url, note, retrieved}. 'observed' = published number; 'inferred' = computed by us from a published dataset (method in note); 'assumption' = a cited rule of thumb we chose to apply. Occupant keys '1'..'5' mean household members, '5' = 5 or more. Climate keys: 'coastal' = Building America 'Marine' zone, 'inland' = Building America 'Hot-Dry' zone (RECS BA_climate); in California RECS 2020 weights, Hot-Dry holds ~9.87 M households and Marine ~3.09 M (Mixed-Dry/Cold together <0.25 M, ignored).
_meta.raw: data/household/raw/recs (microdata, codebook, state PDF, ca_summary.json), raw/epa, raw/web (git-ignored)

ca_avg_annual_kwh.source: U.S. EIA, RECS 2020, 'Annual household site fuel consumption in U.S. homes by state—totals and averages, 2020' (Data release date: March 2023)
ca_avg_annual_kwh.note: California row of the per-household averages table (columns: housing units (million), total electricity (billion kWh), ..., average Electricity (kWh) per household using the fuel), quoted as extracted: 'California 13.18 85.4 390.2 219.9 Q 6482 336 350 Q'. Includes electricity from on-site solar per EIA. 2020 was a COVID year (more time at home). Our microdata cross-check: weighted mean KWH over CA records = 6481.6 kWh.

ca_avg_annual_kwh_by_occupants.units: kWh per household per year (2020), by number of household members
ca_avg_annual_kwh_by_occupants.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
ca_avg_annual_kwh_by_occupants.note: Weighted mean of KWH ('Total electricity use, in kilowatthours, 2020, including self-generation of solar power') by NHSLDMEM ('Number of household members (top-coded)', capped at 5 here). Unweighted sample sizes: {'1': 260, '2': 375, '3': 204, '4': 180, '5': 133}. Codebook: https://www.eia.gov/consumption/residential/data/2020/xls/RECS%202020%20Codebook%20for%20Public%20File%20-%20v7.xlsx

ev_kwh_per_mile.source: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator - Calculations and References (last updated August 4, 2026), section 'Electricity consumed by the average all-electric passenger vehicle'
ev_kwh_per_mile.note: Quoted: 'The weighted average combined electric efficiency of U.S. electric vehicles sales from 2019 and earlier is 3.60 miles per kWh (DOE 2023).' Value = 1/3.60 = 0.278 kWh/mile. Newer/smaller EVs can be more efficient and trucks/SUVs less; cross-check: AFDC home-charging page example uses 'the vehicle consumes 27 kWh to travel 100 miles' (https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity-charging-home).

ev_default_miles_per_day.source: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator - Calculations and References
ev_default_miles_per_day.note: Quoted: 'The average vehicle miles traveled (VMT) in 2022 was 10,917 miles per year and is assumed to be the same for electric cars (FHWA 2024).' 10,917 / 366 days (2024 calendar) = 29.8 mi/day. National, not California-specific.

l2_charger_kw.source: U.S. DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, 'Developing Infrastructure to Charge Electric Vehicles' (Electricity stations)
l2_charger_kw.note: Quoted: 'Most residential Level 2 chargers operate at up to 30 Amps, delivering 7.2 kW of power. These units require a dedicated 40-Amp circuit' and 'A Level 2 unit can range from 2.9 to 19.2 kW power output.' Level 1 for reference: 'Assumes 1.9 kW charging power'. Treat 7.2 kW as charger output; vehicle onboard charger may cap it.

dishwasher_kwh_per_cycle.units: kWh per cycle (electricity at the machine)
dishwasher_kwh_per_cycle.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
dishwasher_kwh_per_cycle.note: Ratio of weighted sums over CA households with a dishwasher (DISHWASH=1, DWASHUSE>0, n=663): sum(KWHDWH) / sum(DWASHUSE x 52). KWHDWH = 'Calibrated electricity usage for dishwashers, in kilowatt-hours, 2020'; DWASHUSE = 'Frequency of dishwasher use per week'. UNCONFIRMED whether RECS counts dishwasher hot-water energy in KWHDWH or in water heating (KWHWTH); treat this as machine energy (motor + heater + dry). Modelled end-use estimates, not metered.

washer_kwh_per_load.units: kWh per load (washer machine energy only)
washer_kwh_per_load.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
washer_kwh_per_load.note: sum(KWHCW) / sum(WASHLOAD x 52) over CA households with a washer and WASHLOAD>0 (n=936). KWHCW = 'Calibrated electricity usage for clothes washers'; WASHLOAD = 'Frequency of clothes washer use per week'. Hot water for washing is NOT included (RECS assigns it to water heating); for an electric water heater add more per warm/hot load.

dryer_kwh_per_load.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
dryer_kwh_per_load.note: sum(KWHCDR) / sum(DRYRUSE x 52) over CA households with an electric dryer (DRYRFUEL=5 'Electricity', DRYRUSE>0, n=461). KWHCDR = 'Calibrated electricity usage for clothes dryers'; DRYRUSE = 'Frequency of clothes dryer use per week'. Gas dryers use only a little electricity (not modelled).

washer_loads_per_week_by_occupants.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
washer_loads_per_week_by_occupants.note: Weighted mean WASHLOAD by NHSLDMEM (5 = 5+) among CA households with a clothes washer (CWASHER=1). n by size: {'1': 170, '2': 328, '3': 174, '4': 157, '5': 117}. All CA washer households: 3.71 loads/week.

dryer_loads_per_week_by_occupants.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
dryer_loads_per_week_by_occupants.note: Weighted mean DRYRUSE by NHSLDMEM (5 = 5+) among CA households that report dryer use (DRYRUSE>=0, any fuel). n by size: {'1': 169, '2': 327, '3': 170, '4': 157, '5': 117}.

dishwasher_cycles_per_week_by_occupants.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
dishwasher_cycles_per_week_by_occupants.note: Weighted mean DWASHUSE by NHSLDMEM (5 = 5+) among CA households with a dishwasher (DISHWASH=1). n by size: {'1': 170, '2': 307, '3': 168, '4': 140, '5': 95}. All CA dishwasher households: 2.60 cycles/week.

cooling_annual_kwh_by_climate.units: kWh per year for space cooling, per household that uses AC (2020)
cooling_annual_kwh_by_climate.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
cooling_annual_kwh_by_climate.note: Weighted mean KWHCOL ('Calibrated electricity usage for space cooling (central air conditioning, individual units, and evaporative coolers)') among CA households with AIRCOND=1, by BA_climate: Marine (coastal) 923 kWh (n=133), Hot-Dry (inland) 1774 kWh (n=690); all CA AC households 1645 kWh. Share of households using AC: Marine 44%, Hot-Dry 81%. Mean CDD65 of the records: Marine 687, Hot-Dry 1801. Caveat: RECS 'Hot-Dry' in CA also covers the LA basin and inland SoCal, so hot Central Valley homes (Fresno, Bakersfield) likely use more; 2020 weather.

cooling_monthly_share.units: fraction of annual cooling kWh by month (Jan..Dec)
cooling_monthly_share.source: PG&E Dynamic Load Profile E1/RES, 2024 (see data/household/load_shapes.json)
cooling_monthly_share.note: Method: monthly kWh of PG&E's average residential customer in 2024 minus the April daily level (minimum month, 13.44 kWh/day) x days; the positive excess in May-Oct is attributed to cooling and normalised to 1. E1 monthly kWh 2024: [525, 460, 446, 403, 442, 558, 736, 600, 528, 495, 467, 532]. Approximation: same seasonal shape for coastal and inland; the excess also contains other summer loads (pool pumps, fans).

cooling_monthly_kwh_by_climate.units: kWh per month for space cooling (Jan..Dec), household with AC
cooling_monthly_kwh_by_climate.source: cooling_annual_kwh_by_climate x cooling_monthly_share (RECS 2020 microdata + PG&E E1 2024 profile)
cooling_monthly_kwh_by_climate.note: Typical-year estimate; coastal = RECS Marine, inland = RECS Hot-Dry. Scale by the user's AC answer; zero if no AC.

cooling_pct_change_per_degF.units: % change in cooling kWh per 1 °F of thermostat setpoint (raise = less energy)
cooling_pct_change_per_degF.source: SMUD (Sacramento Municipal Utility District), 'Heating & Cooling tips'
cooling_pct_change_per_degF.note: Quoted: 'You'll save around 5-10% on cooling costs for every two degrees you raise the temperature.' and 'In the summer months, set your thermostat to 78° or higher.' 5-10% per 2 °F = 2.5-5% per °F; we use the conservative low end, applied linearly to cooling kWh (cap the total change at about +/-25% for large deltas). Cross-check: PG&E summer tips page, quoted: 'You can save as much as 5-10% a year on cooling by simply adjusting your thermostat 7°-10°F degrees higher for 8 hours a day from its normal setting, health permitting. Source: U.S. Department of Energy' (https://www.pge.com/en/save-energy-and-money/energy-usage-and-tips/residential-energy-savings-tips/summer-energy-savings-tips.html).

ac_recommended_setpoint_f.note: Quoted: 'Although 78 degrees is the recommended setting (health permitting) to manage energy use and maintain a comfortable home'. SMUD also says 'set your thermostat to 78° or higher' (https://www.smud.org/Rebates-and-Savings-Tips/Energy-Savings-Tips/Heating-and-Cooling).

electric_heating_annual_kwh_by_climate.units: kWh per year for space heating, household whose main heating fuel is electricity (2020)
electric_heating_annual_kwh_by_climate.source: U.S. EIA, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS) public-use microdata, recs2020_public_v7.csv (California records, state_postal = 'CA', n = 1,152, weighted by final weight NWEIGHT)
electric_heating_annual_kwh_by_climate.note: Weighted mean KWHSPH ('Calibrated electricity usage for space heating, main and secondary') among CA households with FUELHEAT=5 ('Electricity'), by BA_climate: Marine (coastal) 1007 kWh (n=54), Hot-Dry (inland) 779 kWh (n=155); all CA electric-heat households 843 kWh (n=211). By equipment: heat pump (EQUIPM 4 or 13) 758 kWh (n=48); resistance (EQUIPM 5 or 10) 770 kWh (n=105). Most CA homes heat with gas, so these are small samples; mild 2020 winter.

heating_monthly_share.units: fraction of annual heating kWh by month (Jan..Dec)
heating_monthly_share.source: PG&E Dynamic Load Profile E1/RES, 2024 (see data/household/load_shapes.json)
heating_monthly_share.note: Method: as cooling_monthly_share, but the positive excess over the April daily level in Nov-Mar is attributed to heating and normalised to 1. The winter excess also includes longer lighting hours and holiday loads, so this is a rough seasonal shape.

epa_kg_co2e_per_car_mile.units: kg CO2e per mile (average gasoline passenger vehicle)
epa_kg_co2e_per_car_mile.source: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator - Calculations and References (last updated August 4, 2026), 'Miles driven by the average gasoline-powered passenger vehicle'
epa_kg_co2e_per_car_mile.note: Quoted: '8.89 × 10-3 metric tons CO2/gallon gasoline × 1/22.8 miles per gallon car/truck average × 1 CO2, CH4, and N2O/0.994 CO2 = 3.93 x 10-4 metric tons CO2e/mile'. 3.93e-4 t = 0.393 kg. Car-mile equivalent = kg CO2e / 0.393.

epa_kg_co2_per_tree_seedling_10yr.units: kg CO2 per urban tree seedling grown for 10 years (EPA factor, per tree per year)
epa_kg_co2_per_tree_seedling_10yr.source: U.S. EPA, Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator - Calculations and References (last updated August 4, 2026), 'Number of urban tree seedlings grown for 10 years'
epa_kg_co2_per_tree_seedling_10yr.note: Quoted: '36.4 lbs C/tree/year × (44 units CO2/12 units C) × 1 metric ton/2,204.6 lbs = 0.060 metric ton CO2 per urban tree planted per year'. EPA describes 36.4 lbs C as the 'weighted average annual carbon sequestered by a medium growth coniferous or deciduous tree, planted in an urban setting and allowed to grow for 10 years'. Equivalent seedlings = kg CO2e / 60 (EPA's calculator divides by this factor; UNCONFIRMED that the live calculator uses exactly 0.060 rather than an unrounded value).
